implement: legion-worker: the round's rules — the push procedure and handoff trailer, the PR body through skill://legion-worker/references/pr-body.md (the implementer's E2E line and proof array are the Worker Image run log, the in-pod branch `legion probe-image` refusal on today's image, and the pull-request image's rootfs under chroot), and the repository AGENTS.md's image conventions (Debian through mirror.gcr.io, apt unpinned with the suite as the pin, CI builds the image — never docker build in a pod).
test: legion-worker: skill://legion-worker/references/pr-body.md defines what the tester verifies and records — rerun the pull-request image's rootfs checks (the pass, the /usr/bin/jq removal and the /usr/bin/ssh-keygen removal under `unshare -r -m -p -f` + chroot), the in-pod branch-binary refusal and its control, and the subprocess forms of the PATH check; read CI for the Go suites and lint, never rerun the image build.
review: legion-worker: skill://legion-worker/references/merge-gate.md for the review submission; the reviewer reads the two list literals (`go` first), the per-name test table, the apt line, every comment site in the Dockerfile (header, runtime comment, toolchain step and its comment, probe-step comment, the notices preamble that ships in the image and has no automated check), the docs bullet and spot check, and the proofs against the run log.

findings.finding: The pre-merge proof names Stage 4a's image-probe path, which only a devbox operator can run (docker, a cluster context under the daemon's identity, the secrets CLI); a pod cannot create pods or exec.
findings.answer: Departure 1: the implementer proves the same probe code path on the pull request's Worker Image run (the image's own `legion probe-image`), the branch `legion probe-image` in its own pod, and the published sha-<12> image's rootfs under chroot; Stage 4a is not required for completion and is the architect's to ask of the operator lane (decision 2).

findings.finding: The production check's pod-side commands have no runner: the implementer cannot exec into a pod created after the pin and its own pod predates it.
findings.answer: Production check item 1 reads the daemon's `the worker image passed its probe` log line in legion-system (pods/log is permitted), whose log tail carries the toolchain row with /usr/bin/jq and /usr/bin/ssh-keygen; item 2 lists issue pods by imageID and asks a live role of a post-pin pod over Envoy to run the four commands and `bun test scripts/e2e/lib/`; which role is decision 1 for the architect.

findings.finding: `command -v jq` in the harness bash answers for its builtin (measured: prints `jq`, exit 0, with no /usr/bin/jq), so the spec's `command -v jq ssh-keygen` check decides nothing.
findings.answer: Departure 2: every PATH check is a subprocess form — `bash -c 'type -P jq ssh-keygen'`, `env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin sh -c 'command -v jq ssh-keygen'`, `/usr/bin/env jq --version`, `test -x /usr/bin/jq -a -x /usr/bin/ssh-keygen`; `! test -e /tmp/jq` and a PATH with no /tmp element check 'no jq fetched to /tmp'.

findings.finding: `bun test scripts/e2e/lib/` cannot pass in any pod: two tests in nats-stream.test.ts spawn docker.
findings.answer: Departure 3: the measured expectation is 315 pass, 2 fail (both nats-stream.test.ts), and no output matching `jq: command not found` or `Executable not found in $PATH: "jq"`; the 8 ensure-project.test.ts cases (harness PATH pinned to /usr/bin:/bin) are the sharpest signal that an apt-installed /usr/bin/jq is what fixes it.

findings.finding: The pre-merge bun-test proof needs a real /usr/bin/jq in the workspace's own environment, which the chroot of a separate rootfs does not give.
findings.answer: The bun-test criterion is a production-check item (post-pin pod); pre-merge evidence is the probe table, the toolchain step's output and the rootfs checks, plus the measured baseline (212 fail without jq; 307 pass with a /tmp jq; 8 more need /usr/bin/jq).

findings.finding: The third-party-notices preamble (worker.Dockerfile:418, text shipped in the image) enumerates the Debian packages by name and nothing automated checks it.
findings.answer: The change's step 3 names it: '… the chromium, python3, curl, wget, jq and openssh-client of the capability check'; the reviewer reads it (its own item in 'What the reviewer reads').

findings.finding: Nine sites name the Debian package list or the toolchain binary list, not the spec's three; three more deliberately do not.
findings.answer: The plan lists every site to change (apt line, runtime comment, header paragraph, notices preamble, toolchain step and comment, probe-step comment, image.go names, capabilities.go summary, docs/kubernetes.md bullet and probe subsection with its spot check) and every site left as is with why (running-legion.md's non-exhaustive summary, the size figures, the image-row list, the contracts fixture).

findings.finding: The Dockerfile's toolchain RUN step runs every capability-checked command and the spec never mentions it; ssh-keygen takes no --version.
findings.answer: Step 3 adds `jq --version` and a scratch-directory key generation (`ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -N '' -f "$scratch/probe-key"; ssh-keygen -l -f "$scratch/probe-key.pub"`) with one comment sentence, as the step does for gofmt, pnpx and socat.

findings.finding: Test shape: two stub lists, one expected detail string, and the `paths[0]` invariant (`go` first) constrain where the names go.
findings.answer: Append `jq`, `ssh-keygen` after `kubectl`; add both to `stubBinaries` and `imageBinaries`; extend the expected Toolchain detail at image_test.go:155; turn TestCheckImageNamesTheOneBinaryOffPATH into a per-name table (python3, jq, ssh-keygen) so a name forgotten from the list fails; no new probe_image_test case (python3's already proves the toolchain row's exit path); no fixture change.

findings.finding: The spec's negative control (a rootfs with /usr/bin/jq removed) is reachable only once the pull request's image exists; a cheaper control proves the same earlier.
findings.answer: AC2 names both: the implementer-owned branch `legion probe-image` on today's image in its pod (`capability toolchain is missing: jq, ssh-keygen are not on PATH`, exit 1; the pod's own legion passes as the control), and the rootfs removal on the published image for the implementer and the tester.

findings.finding: openssh-client also ships ssh, scp, sftp, ssh-agent and ssh-add, which the spec never says; no Debian package carries ssh-keygen alone.
findings.answer: Accepted in the plan (risks) and the row checks ssh-keygen alone; decision 3 offers the architect to record it in the spec.

findings.finding: Four claims rest on nothing in the tree: the trixie package versions and dependency closure, the harness jq builtin, the pod measurements, and the absence of a hadolint job.
findings.answer: Each is cited to its source in the plan: the Worker Image run's apt output for the versions and closure, this planner's pod transcript for the builtin and the missing binaries, and `grep hadolint` over .github finding nothing — the build's own final RUN is the gate, not a linter.

findings.finding: The apt line is the runtime stage's first RUN, so the one-line change rebuilds every later layer; a toomanyrequests red is the known registry window.
findings.answer: Named in step 3 and the risks: rerun the Worker Image job once with `gh run rerun <id> --failed`; image growth is on the order of 10 MB.

specDepartures.spec: Proof: 'Before the merge, the implementer proves the same in the Stage 4a image probe path the repository's scripts/e2e/README.md describes.'
specDepartures.plan: The implementer proves the same `legion probe-image` code path on the pull request's Worker Image run (the image's own probe as its last build step), on the branch `legion probe-image` in its own pod (refusal by name on today's image), and on the published sha-<12> image's rootfs under chroot in the pod (pass, then the /usr/bin/jq removal). Stage 4a's image-probe on this digest is not required for completion; the architect may ask the operator lane for it as in PR #1846.
specDepartures.evidence: scripts/e2e/README.md lines 537-541: Stage 4a is devbox-only and needs docker, a cluster context under the daemon's identity and the secrets CLI; measured in this pod: no docker, `kubectl auth can-i create pods -n legion` and `create pods/exec` both no; `unshare -r -m -p -f` + /usr/sbin/chroot runs a copied rootfs's omp here, and the anonymous ghcr token fetches the image manifest (22 layers, ~1.05 GB).

specDepartures.spec: Proof: '`command -v jq ssh-keygen` prints two /usr/bin paths' as the pod-side check.
specDepartures.plan: Subprocess forms decide the criterion: `bash -c 'type -P jq ssh-keygen'`, `env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin sh -c 'command -v jq ssh-keygen'`, `/usr/bin/env jq --version`, `test -x /usr/bin/jq -a -x /usr/bin/ssh-keygen`.
specDepartures.evidence: Measured in this pod on an image with no /usr/bin/jq: `command -v jq ssh-keygen` in the harness bash prints `jq` and exits 0 (the builtin answers), while the subprocess forms exit 127 and 1.

specDepartures.spec: Proof: '`bun test scripts/e2e/lib/` passes in that pod with no jq fetched to /tmp.'
specDepartures.plan: Expected 315 pass, 2 fail, both failures in scripts/e2e/lib/nats-stream.test.ts (it spawns docker, absent from every pod), and no output matching `jq: command not found` or `Executable not found in $PATH: "jq"`.
specDepartures.evidence: Measured in this pod after `bun install --frozen-lockfile`: 105 pass / 212 fail of 317 without jq, every failure naming jq; 307 pass / 10 fail with a /tmp jq first on PATH — 8 in ensure-project.test.ts (harness PATH `${dir}:/usr/bin:/bin`, line 72, so only /usr/bin/jq satisfies them) and 2 in nats-stream.test.ts (Bun.spawnSync(["docker", …]), lines 23-27).
